scope: Descriptive external comparison of frozen v0.7.16 motion; no optimization on these recordings.

walking.modelInference: FlyBody fits 13 top-view 2D landmarks, including six leg tips; knee locations and vertical swing paths are inferred, not directly tracked 3D joints. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12310536/#Sec20
walking.metric: Physical femur–tibia interior angle between three landmarks; Wasserstein distribution distance in degrees. Foot spread is RMS claw displacement relative to coxa, centered on its mean, divided by median femur length.
walking.limitations: Different individuals, recording contexts, speeds and durations; no synchronized frames, foot-contact forces or matched locomotor condition. Distribution distance is not pointwise reconstruction error. Three flies are insufficient for a general population accuracy claim.

flight.metric: Published annotated haltere frequency; Welch dominant frequency of the longest finite untreated wing signal (at least 1 s), 100–min(350,0.45fs) Hz search band. Both are recording-level summaries.
flight.limitations: Tethered flight. Repeated recordings from the same flies; no independent-individual confidence interval. The supplied fly identifier table is MATLAB opaque and not decoded here. The haltere file lacks the README-described treat field: untreatedanimal is the supplied inclusion flag. Lateral 2D haltere angles and normalized wing signals cannot validate 3D wing trajectories or our haltere joint excursion.

failures: No matched free-walking or free-flight ground truth for this individual.
No full 3D wing trajectory error, ground contact/slip error, neural controller validation, or physiological validation.
Photo-guided material changes have no calibrated color/reflectance error.
Drosophila simulans in the 2026 Diptera archive excluded from species-specific comparison.
interpretation: Do not interpret a frequency inside an observed range as proof of accurate flight. This audit can reveal mismatch, not establish universal biological validity.
